description_full: Spirax Group plc provides thermal energy and fluid technology solutions in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, and the Americas. It operates through three segments: Steam Thermal Solutions, Electric Thermal Solutions, and Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions. The company offers industrial and commercial steam systems, including condensate management, controls, and thermal energy management products and solutions for heating, curing, cooking, drying, cleaning, sterilizing, space heating, humidifying, vacuum packing, and producing hot water; electrical process heating and temperature management solutions, such as industrial heaters and systems, heat tracing, and various component technologies; and designs and manufactures peristaltic and niche pumps and associated fluid path technologies, including tubing, specialised filling systems and products for single use applications. The company serves food and beverage, pharmaceutical and biotechnology, oil and gas, chemical, power generation, healthcare, buildings, water and wastewater, semiconductor, transport, original equipment manufacturers machinery, and mining and precious metal processing industries. The company was formerly known as Spirax-Sarco Engineering plc and changed its name to Spirax Group PLC in June 2024. Spirax Group PLC was founded in 1888 and is headquartered in Cheltenham, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: SPIRAX GROUP PLC is a mid-cap industrials business with a $7.3B market cap on $2.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 12% against a 7% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 76% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $305M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.81× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.6×.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

val: The stock trades only 3% below its DCF fair value of $101, a thin margin of safety.

hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.8x net debt to EBITDA ($492.8M of cash against $1.4B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 5.6x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.1, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 4.1% over 3 years.

own: Insiders hold little stock (0.5%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 2.2% a year to shareholders (2.3% in dividends).
people: With about 10,000 employees, each generates about $227K of revenue, 0.6x the Industrials median.
That works out to $30K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.1M (9x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
